# TreeStore clear() and reloads are quadratic in the visible node count

## Context

Clearing a `TreeStore` takes time quadratic in its visible node count. `Store#afterSetData()` clears before it adds, so every data reload of a large flat or expanded tree pays the same cost.

Measured on `dev` `5dcacbe` with a unit probe (Turbo Mode, Node, ms):

| Case | `clear()` / reload |
|---|---|
| `TreeStore`, 10,000 flat visible nodes | 75 |
| `TreeStore`, 20,000 flat visible nodes | 639 |
| `TreeStore`, 40,000 flat visible nodes | 1,769 |
| `Store`, 40,000 rows (control) | 0 |
| `TreeStore`, 50 × 800 collapsed, 50 visible (control) | 1 |
| `TreeStore`, 50 × 800 expanded, 40,050 visible | 777 |
| `TreeStore`, 40,000 flat, `store.data = rows` | 1,532 |

## The Problem

`TreeStore#splice()` runs two O(N) scans once per removed node:

1. Step 1b decides visibility with `me.indexOf(node) > -1`. `Collection#indexOf()` is `_items.indexOf(...)`, a scan of the projection.
2. The removal reaches `Collection#splice()` as an array of items, whose per-item path runs `items.splice(me.indexOfKey(key), 1)`: a scan plus a shift for each item. `clear()` arrives as the numeric form `splice(0, count)`, and the override converts it to that array form (`_items.slice(...)`), so the Collection's one-pass numeric path is never taken.

Each scan is quadratic on its own. At 40,000 flat visible nodes, fixing only the first leaves `clear()` at 1,580 ms. Fixing only the second leaves 501 ms, still quadratic (52, 197, 501 ms at 10k, 20k, 40k). Fixing both gives 31 ms, and the reload drops from 1,532 to 85 ms.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/TreeStore.mjs` `clear()` wipes `#allRecordsMap` and `#childrenMap`, then calls `super.clear()`. That reaches `Collection#clear()`, whose `this.splice(0, this.count)` dispatches back into the `splice()` override.
- `splice()` step 1b: `if (me.indexOf(node) > -1) visibleToRemove.push(node)`. Step 4: `super.splice(insertIndex, visibleToRemove, visibleToAdd, silent)`.
- The projection's key map, `me.map`, holds exactly the visible keys (`#rebuildKeysAndCount()` rebuilds it from `_items`), and `Collection#splice()` removes by key. `map.has(key)` therefore answers the same question in O(1).
- Design authority: the `TreeStore#addChild` JSDoc, "Ingestion is already O(N) over a level, so a per-node key scan makes a bulk load O(N²) … in the one class whose whole premise is 50k-record ingestion."

## The Fix

In `TreeStore#splice()`:

1. Step 1b: `me.map.has(key)` instead of `me.indexOf(node) > -1`.
2. Step 4: when the call removes the whole projection (`index === 0 && removeCountOrToRemoveArray === me.count`), delegate the numeric form, `super.splice(0, me.count, visibleToAdd, silent)`, so the Collection drops the projection in one pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `clear()` on a `TreeStore` resolves no node position by scanning. A spec counts `indexOf` / `indexOfKey` calls during `clear()` of a flat and of an expanded tree and expects none; on `dev` it counts one or more per visible node.
- [ ] AC-2: `clear()` and a data reload leave the state they leave on `dev` and fire the same `mutate` payload: count 0, nothing reachable through `get()` or `getChildren()`, and the removed items in projection order.
- [ ] AC-3: The existing `TreeStore` specs and the unit tier pass.
- [ ] AC-4: The PR body carries this table re-measured at its head commit.

## Out of Scope

- Bulk removal of a non-contiguous subset (`store.remove(manyNodes)`). The Collection's array removal stays per-item, here and for plain `Store`s; it gets its own ticket if measured to matter.
- Step 2a's `me.indexOf(parentNode)` check when adding under an expanded parent, which is not on the clear path.

## Related

- `TreeStore#addChild`: the same class's bulk-load O(N²) fix, and the precedent for measuring at 20k+ nodes.
- #9432: the `clear()` override against the split-brain leak. Its requirement that `clear()` calls `super.clear()` holds under this fix.
- #9404: the Tree Grid epic. It is past the sub-issue cap, so this stays standalone.
